correctness.rationale: For any integer m>=3, real lambda>0, binary equal-edge-interest best responses on the labeled wheel reduce to 2k>=lambda+2 for a hub-matching rim site and lambda+2>=2ell for a hub-opposing rim site. This yields cyclic 2/3-spacing of zeros below lambda=2, isolated zeros at equality, and no zeros above. Cyclic gap root counting gives refined 2m/z*binom(z,m-2z), the closed-walk transfer trace gives Perrin P_m, and independent sets of a cycle give Lucas L_m at equality. Strict hub ties occur in exactly four even-m alternations below threshold; all states tie at threshold; two strong equilibria above. Each all-profile cut has edge weight lambda(m-z)+rim transitions. Eliminating consecutive zeros raises cut, then maximizing z proves max cut lambda*m+(2-lambda)_+floor(m/2), PoS=1 and stated PoA and asymptotic entropy. Independent direct payoff enumeration covered m=3..10 at four rational weights on both sides and at threshold; source verifier covers m=3..14. These finite tests do not prove the all-m theorem.
residual_risks: Real lambda quantified by analytic strict inequalities, not by tested rational weights
The low-lambda count uses labeled profiles and treats hub inversion as distinct; changing the equivalence convention changes multiplicities

originality.rationale: The game is equivalent to single-spin-flip local maxima of an antiferromagnetic weighted wheel cut. The Perrin and Lucas recurrences and generic maximum-cut/PNE relationship are prior tools, not novel by themselves. The surviving result is the full three-regime wheel classification including strict equilibria and sharp welfare inefficiency; the inspected ladder and general anti-coordination treatments do not directly imply it. The most dangerous wheel-specific Ising paper studies ground-state degeneration (global energy minimizers), a different object from all local equilibria, but its uninspected technical material remains a real priority risk.
